description: Builds a pass/fail LLM-as-a-judge prompt for one kind of AI step (make, answer, transform, extract, judge, find, predict, plan, act or learn). Returns the prompt with {{input}} and {{result}} placeholders, numbered pass conditions (the block's starter conditions unless you send your own), up to 3 pass and 3 fail examples interleaved, and a JSON or XML answer format.

block.description: What the AI step does. make: creates new content from a request (an image, a post, slides, advice); answer: replies to a question that has a right answer (a support reply, a policy question, a how-to); transform: reshapes material faithfully (a rewrite, a translation, text to speech); extract: pulls out what's in the input (fields from a PDF, speech to text, text from a photo); judge: gives a label, score or choice that can be checked now (moderation, routing, a guardrail); find: picks the few relevant items out of many (search, recommendations); predict: makes an estimate that can only be checked later (will this lead buy, is this fraud, when will it arrive); plan: turns a goal into steps (a research plan, a multi-step task); act: takes one action with side effects (send an email, take a payment, call an API); learn: updates a model or prompt from examples (a voice clone, prompt tuning).

criteria.description: Pass conditions, one per item. Omitted: the starter conditions for the block.

failedExamples.description: Real results that didn't work; labelled fail in the prompt

result.description: What the step produced, in full

featureDescription.description: Who uses the feature, what they ask for and what a good result gives them

includeReasoning.description: Whether the judge writes a short reason before its verdict

workedExamples.description: Real results that worked first time; labelled pass in the prompt

result.description: What the step produced, in full

title: Judge prompt builder

description: Compares a person's verdicts with an AI judge's verdicts on the same results. Returns the agreement rate, Cohen's kappa with confidence intervals, precision and recall per verdict, the agreement of a judge that always gives the most common verdict, a trust verdict (kappa 0.6 or more with at least 80% recall on every verdict; 0.4 to 0.6 is borderline; under 30 results is too few) and the rows where the two disagree.

csv.description: The same data as CSV or TSV text instead of rows: columns named human and judge (and optionally note), or the first two columns in that order.

rows.description: One row per result. Common words are mapped onto two verdicts: worked (worked, pass, yes, true, 1, good, kept, accepted, ok) and didn't work (didn't work, fail, no, false, 0, bad, redo, retry, rejected, wrong). Other labels are compared as written.

human.description: The person's verdict on one result

judge.description: The AI judge's verdict on the same result

note.description: What the result was, to recognise it in the disagreements

name: judge_agreement

agreement.description: Share of results where the judge and the person gave the same verdict

alwaysSameVerdict.description: The agreement a judge would get by always giving the most common human verdict

disagreements.description: The first 25 results where the verdicts differ

kappa.description: Cohen's kappa: agreement beyond chance. Null when it is undefined.

kappaBand.description: Landis and Koch label for kappa

judged.description: Results the judge gave this verdict

precision.description: Of the results the judge gave this verdict, share the person agreed with

recall.description: Of the results the person gave this verdict, share the judge also gave

support.description: Results the person gave this verdict
